newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia banks want more freedom to trade gold.
newsitem.headline: Russia banks want more freedom to trade gold.

text.p: Russian banks on Tuesday called for more freedom to trade gold at home and abroad in exchange for providing funds for the ailing gold mining industry.

"Even after all government resolutions (on liberalising the gold market), the state in effect is limiting banks' gold operations both on the domestic and on the international markets, preserving its monopoly," a news release from the Association of Russian Banks said.
The association said the government should let the central bank sell gold to commercial banks for export, and allow commercial banks to export gold mined at their own cost.
The banks also want the government to substitute direct funding of the industry from the budget by a new mechanism, involving commercial banks.

"The government may find ways to fund the banks in the form of gold from the state funds, while the banks will convert the gold into money for the mining industry," Vladimir Vinogradov, President of Inkombank, told a news conference.
The government, in a budget crisis and facing a tax revenue shortfall, has even less money this year to finance output, and 1996 production will not better 1995's poor 125-132 tonnes.
Russia's gold mines, even those run by foreign joint ventures, are required to sell their output to the state at fixed prices and are usually paid many months later.
Commercial banks financed only about five tonnes of output last year. Moscow has promised but done little to let banks with special licences take gold abroad to secure financing.
Bankers said they wanted the central bank to sign forward gold contracts with major banks investing in the industry.

The central bank's new rules, issued last month, would allow banks to trade gold domestically in a limited way through special precious metal accounts and to make and secure limited, gold-backed loans.

Two gold exchanges are being set up in Russia, while a diamond exchange is already working. The government has issued licences alowing more than 120 commercial banks to buy and sell gold domestically and a total of five banks have been allowed to trade gold abroad.

But while banks demand more freedom in gold trade, the head of Russia's recently-dissolved State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones said Russia's gold and diamond market was already one of the most liberal of all.
"Russia's gold market is now more liberal then anywhere in the world," said Yuri Kotlyar, whose commmittee, once a precious metals monopoly, is under reorganisation.
"We have more than 120 banks authorised to work with gold internally, while in Italy they have only four such banks," he told Reuters.

But he said the draft law on precious metals and stones, giving producers the right to own part of their production, had yet to be passed through parliament and signed into law and called for more gold and diamond exchanges to be set up.
The law which would have given gold mines more control over output and sales was vetoed by President Boris Yeltsin in July.
